It does not cover housing, meals, or parking. Support for an individual student must not exceed three years.
programs.eligibility: U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents who are full-time students at a participating school, typically within three years of graduating: a junior or senior in a bachelor’s program, a master’s student, or a research-based doctoral student. Community college sophomores are eligible for one year of support if there is a formal agreement with a four-year participating school that will accept the transfer, then two additional years of support. Awards are merit-based, not based on financial need. There is no veteran-only track, and spouses and family are not a special category. Veterans qualify like any other student. Recipients must meet federal employment and suitability rules and may need a security clearance.
programs.what_you_get: CyberAICorps Scholarship for Service (CyberAI SFS), run by the U.S. National Science Foundation with the U.S. Office of Personnel Management and the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, pays tuition and mandatory education fees for up to three years, plus a stipend of $27,000 a year for undergraduates or $37,000 a year for graduate students, and a $6,000 professional allowance each academic year. After you graduate, you must work in AI or cybersecurity at a qualified government organization for at least as long as you received the scholarship. A required summer internship is part of the scholarship. If you do not meet the academic or service requirements, the award must be repaid or converted to a student loan. The program was renamed from CyberCorps Scholarship for Service in 2026; OPM’s site still uses the CyberCorps name. It is not limited to veterans, and it is not a free certification. Housing, meals, and parking are not covered. Apply through a participating school; there is no single national application.
